$comment: Turning wire bytes into text, shared by tests/shared/decoding.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. IRC never agreed on an encoding: UTF-8 won wherever it was allowed to, but EFnet and IRCnet have no UTF8ONLY and never will, and both clients decoded strictly as UTF-8 — so a Latin-1 line arrived as a row of replacement characters with nothing to say whose fault it was.
$cases: `bytes` is hex, exactly as the line arrived. `text` is what it should read as.

cases.name: an emoji, which only UTF-8 can carry
Latin-1, which is not valid UTF-8, reads as the accent it meant
a Windows curly quote, in the range ISO-8859-1 leaves unassigned
an em dash from an old Windows client
a truncated multi-byte sequence is not UTF-8
an overlong encoding of a slash is not UTF-8 either
a lone surrogate half has no UTF-8 encoding
